summary: Loomis packs fewer than 7,000 people into just over seven square miles of rolling Sierra Nevada foothill terrain east of Sacramento, yet it sits along the Interstate 80 corridor — meaning a commute into downtown Sacramento runs roughly 25 miles, while a weekend drive to Lake Tahoe is barely 90 minutes up the same highway. That foothill geography matters daily: elevations around 400–500 feet give the landscape a gentle oak-woodland character with western views toward the Sacramento Valley floor, and summer highs averaging 75°F with 9.3 hours of daily sunshine make the dry heat manageable compared to the valley below. At a density of 935 people per square mile, the pacing is decidedly rural-suburban — no real downtown bustle, more horse properties and hobby ranches than mixed-use corridors. The median home value of roughly $650,000 against a median household income near $103,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 6.3, which is steep but notably less punishing than Sacramento's inner suburbs; median rent at $1,741 tells a similar story. Loomis functions almost entirely as a bedroom community, with most employment in healthcare, education, and government concentrated in Roseville and Sacramento proper. The town's identity orbits around its agricultural roots — the annual Eggplant Festival is a real, longstanding event — and a small historic stretch near the rail line offers a handful of local shops and eateries rather than chain sprawl. It is, in essence, a place where the commute is the price of admission for foothill quiet and open sky.
